cloze.s: The small museum is funded ___ by ticket sales and receives no grants or donations of any kind.

why: Old cloze was self-contradictory ('wholly due to volunteers' but paid staff did 'very little'), and wrong option 'predominantly' fit it better than the answer

set.def: the inner reason or desire that makes someone act in a particular way

why: Def said 'especially one that is hidden' -- motive does not imply hidden (that is 'ulterior motive'); misleading

set.def: to pay someone for a loss, injury, or work, or to make up for a weakness or lack

why: Def covered only the payment sense, but example 2 ('compensate for her late start') uses the make-up-for sense

set.def: by your own free choice, without being forced or required to act

why: 'without being ... paid' is not part of the adverb's meaning (company 'voluntarily recalled' toys has nothing to do with pay)

cloze.s: The soup wasn't ___ hot, so Hannah put it back in the microwave for another minute.

why: Old cloze 'had ___ recovered from the flu' also fits wrong options 'wholly' and 'substantially'

cloze.s: The defender ___ kicked the ball out of bounds so that an injured opponent could get medical help.

why: Old cloze ('kicked the ball out of bounds to stop the clock') describes no real sport rule; inaccurate
'readily kicked the ball out' (willingly) could fit the cloze
'record-breaking' is not a synonym -- breaking a record implies earlier precedents exist
'whimsical' means playfully fanciful in current use, not a true synonym of arbitrary
'comprehensive' is a synonym only of the 'including everything' sense, not the welcoming sense defined
'accountability' is a related idea, not a synonym
'eloquence' is positive and does not match the def's 'lacking substance' sense
'abandon' is not a synonym of neglect (leaving entirely vs failing to care for)
'deliberation' is the noun of the verb sense, not of the adjective taught here

cloze.s: Forgetting to attach the file was an honest ___, and Maria sent the email again right away.

why: 'resent' reads as 'resented'; ambiguous wording
'Without ample/explicit reasons to change the plan' also fits the cloze
'so paramount to the city's traffic' is a plausible fill; meanings overlap (central/most important)
'no longer robust as a business' is a plausible cloze fill; def overlap (works well/survives)
'Without any compelling evidence' fits the cloze; 'convincing' overlaps 'able to be believed'
'The author's explicit descriptions' could fill the cloze
'completely arbitrary; nobody had planned it' fits cloze; arbitrary def ('personal whim') overlaps
'tired of empty speculation and wanted concrete plans' fits the cloze
discretion def 'the freedom to decide what to do' overlaps autonomy; 'gave him the discretion to set his own hours' fits the cloze
Commonly confused with irony (the item's own note says so); 'twist of coincidence' arguable fill
'the motive that pushed Kwame to start his own business' fits the cloze
'had to undergo/confront weeks of violent storms' fits the cloze; undergo def overlaps endure
'quick to confront the cruel online posts' is a plausible fill
'forgot to set his alarm and inevitably arrived an hour late' fits the cloze
'substantially residential' fits the cloze
'The diet arguably helps you lose ten pounds' fits; both hedge a claim -- (b) ambiguous for learners
'travel times dropped remarkably' is a plausible fill
'the two doctors fundamentally agree' fits the cloze
'No single donor gave much, but remarkably the neighbors raised enough' fits the cloze
